Create Time-Series Trend Plots from GTAP Data

Source: R/plot.R
trend_plot.Rd

Generates line plots to visualize trends over time across multiple dimensions, with flexible grouping, splitting, and styling options.

Usage

trend_plot(
  data,
  filter_var = NULL,
  panel_var,
  group_by,
  split_by = NULL,
  variable_col = "Variable",
  unit_col = "Unit",
  desc_col = "Description",
  invert_pane = FALSE,
  separate_figure = FALSE,
  var_name_by_description = FALSE,
  add_var_info = FALSE,
  output_path = NULL,
  export_picture = TRUE,
  export_as_pdf = FALSE,
  export_config = NULL,
  plot_style_config = NULL,
  line_size = 1.5,
  add_points = TRUE,
  point_size = 3,
  add_smooth = FALSE,
  smooth_method = "loess",
  vertical_lines = NULL,
  add_average_line = FALSE,
  avg_line_color = "red",
  avg_line_size = 1,
  avg_line_type = "dashed",
  avg_line_label = "Average"
)

Arguments

data

A data frame or a list of data frames containing GTAP results.

filter_var

Vector or data frame. If a vector, filters the values in `group_by`. If a data frame, filters `variable_col` based on matching values.

panel_var

Character. Column containing time variable for x-axis (e.g., "Year").

group_by

Character. Column for grouping lines (e.g., "REG" or "Country").

split_by

Character or vector. Column name(s) for data splitting (e.g., "COMM"). Set to NULL for no splitting, suitable for macro-level analysis.

variable_col

Character. Column containing variable identifiers (default: "Variable").

unit_col

Character. Column containing unit information (default: "Unit").

desc_col

Character. Column containing variable descriptions (default: "Description").

invert_pane

Logical. If TRUE, creates horizontal trend lines (default: FALSE).

separate_figure

Logical. If TRUE, generates separate figures per variable (default: FALSE).

var_name_by_description

Logical. If TRUE, uses descriptions instead of variable codes (default: FALSE).

add_var_info

Logical. If TRUE, adds variable code in parentheses after description (default: FALSE).

output_path

Character. Directory path for saving output files. If NULL, plots are only returned.

export_picture

Logical. If TRUE, exports plots as image files (default: TRUE).

export_as_pdf

Logical or "merged". If TRUE, exports separate PDFs; if "merged", creates a multi-page PDF.

export_config

List. Export settings like width, height, and file name.

plot_style_config

List. Custom plot styles (see `?get_plot_style_config`).

line_size

Numeric. Thickness of trend lines (default: 1.5).

add_points

Logical. If TRUE, adds point markers at each data point (default: TRUE).

point_size

Numeric. Size of point markers (default: 3).

add_smooth

Logical. If TRUE, adds smoothed trend lines (default: FALSE).

smooth_method

Character. Method for smoothing ("loess", "lm", etc.) (default: "loess").

vertical_lines

Named list. Specifications for vertical reference lines, each containing: - position: Numeric. X-axis position for the vertical line - color: Character. Color of the line - linetype: Character. Line type (e.g., "dashed", "solid") - size: Numeric. Line thickness - text: Character. Optional label for the line - text_size: Numeric. Size of the text label - text_angle: Numeric. Angle of the text label (default: 90) - text_color: Character. Color of the text label (defaults to line color) - x_offset: Numeric. Horizontal offset for the text label - y_offset: Numeric. Vertical position for the text label

add_average_line

Logical. If TRUE, adds a line showing average values (default: FALSE).

avg_line_color

Character. Color for the average line (default: "red").

avg_line_size

Numeric. Thickness for the average line (default: 1).

avg_line_type

Character. Line type for the average line (default: "dashed").

avg_line_label

Character. Label for the average line (default: "Average").

Value

A list of ggplot2 objects (invisibly) containing the generated plots.

Examples

# \donttest{
# Basic trend plot with vertical reference lines
trend_plot(
  data = time_series_data,
  panel_var = "Year",
  group_by = "Region",
  vertical_lines = list(
    recession = list(
      position = 2008,
      color = "red",
      linetype = "dashed",
      text = "2008 Recession",
      text_angle = 90
    ),
    policy_change = list(
      position = 2015,
      color = "blue",
      text = "Policy Change"
    )
  ),
  add_average_line = TRUE
)
#> Error: object 'time_series_data' not found
# }
